text:
elaine: Heads up — saw steady mem growth on a long-running streamed chat session. After ~1500 tokens heap + GPU pinned memory climb and eventually OOM on one pod. suspect kvcache retention across request boundaries when batch splits happen.

alex: ugh. any repro?

elaine: minimal repro attached here (ran locally):
```
# start a long stream with variable chunking
python tools/bench_stream.py --model redwood/open-7b --seq 2000 --chunk 128 --concurrency 1
```
logs:
```
2026-02-11T14:12:03Z INFO request=abc123 batch_split=true kv_pages_alloc=4096 kv_pages_active=4096
2026-02-11T14:12:10Z WARN request=def456 kv_pages_active=4256 stale_blocks=3
2026-02-11T14:12:30Z ERROR oom pod-12 kv_mem_used=11.6GB
```

elaine: note the stale_blocks metric — that's our new probe counting fragment headers with mismatched request_id.

maria: I tried reproing locally, hit something similar but only when the kernel selector flipped to matmul-f16 mid-session (small kernel-switch). Could be ordering of kv append + kernel switch.

sam: can you paste a short trace? flamegraphs help.

elaine: pasted CPU profile gist: https://gists.example.com/xx/railshift-flame (private). quick stack hits: 
- kv_store::append_page
- kv_store::tag_page
- runtime::select_kernel
- runtime::execute_step

elaine: hypothesis: when batching heuristics split a batch we sometimes leave a half-filled page tagged with the previous request id, then next request reuses the page but the tag isn't rewritten because of a fast-path reuse; alignment offset remains from prior request -> misaligned token offsets.

alex: that would explain wrong token alignment and cross-request contamination. any small patch idea?

maria: two quick safe guards: 1) zero the page header on claim 2) make claim() take a hard fence when the kernel changes. both will cost perf but narrow scope.

sam: can we repro with N=2 sessions hitting kernel switch path quickly? I'll run stress on a ded pool.

perf-bot: alert: KV_CACHE_STALE_BLOCKS spike on ded-pool-7 at 2026-02-11T14:11:59Z (+1200% over baseline) :rotating_light:

alex: ok I'm going to prototype header zeroing on page-claim in a feature flag guarded change. If perf hit is significant we can instead do a header-compare-and-write only when tag mismatch detected.

elaine: also saw corruption when quantized kernel chooses different page-size. we should add an invariant check at eviction: verify page.tag == request_id or page.last_used < now-ttl. if mismatch log a dump (no crash).

maria: I added a unit test sketch:
```python
def test_page_claim_reuse_alignment():
    store = KVStore(page_size=4096)
    page = store.claim_page(request_id="r1")
    page.write_tokens(b"...", offset=64)
    # simulate fast-return and kernel switch path
    page.mark_active(False)
    page2 = store.claim_page(request_id="r2")
    assert page2.offset == 0  # must be fresh start
```

sam: looks good. also add an e2e that runs long stream and asserts never to see stale_blocks > 0 after a kernel switch event.

alex: pushed prototype w/ flag kvcache.strict_claim=true to my branch alex/kv-railshift. patch: zero page header on claim and increment generation counter on kernel switch.

elaine: tested on ded-pool staging -> reduced stale_blocks to 0 over a 30m run but average latency up ~2.3% and throughput -1.8% on heavy batching cases. acceptable for safety, but want to avoid permanent regressions.

maria: next idea: avoid zeroing every time — maintain per-page generation counter. on kernel switch bump a global generation, on claim if page.gen != global_gen then wipe header; else fast path. that avoids most claims paying cost.

alex: implemented gen approach in branch alex/kv-gen-guard. perf test shows overhead only when kernel switches (~0.1% steady).

sam: excellent. can we also add metrics: page_gen_mismatch_count and page_zero_count so SRE can monitor?

elaine: yes please. also we should add a nightly long-context regression run that exercises kernel switching + small batch splits — current CI covers short chats only.

maria: I'll prepare the unit+e2e tests and a small fuzz that randomizes batch split boundaries to catch other races.

alex: creating PR now, request reviews from @maria and @sam. PR includes: gen guard, metric, invariant-check logging, and tests.

elaine: thanks. once merged let's run a few 24h long runs on staging and then promote to a canary in prod.

sam: noted, I'll schedule canary windows and add rollback playbook steps in case of perf regressions.

perf-bot: test-run summary: staging/ded-pool run (2h) zero stale_blocks, mem growth plateaued at expected baseline.

elaine: nice. leaving followups in the PR. :thumbsup:
